trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is automatic: it unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are earned. There is no separate task. Follow the roadmap in order — story first, then side strands, activities, collectibles, and the money and combat clean-up — and use the checklist to see what is left. The 100% completion trophy (A Long Road) is the usual last step before this one pops.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game Stats menu (trophy progress)

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this trophy cannot be missed on a normal playthrough — just play through the opening and it pops when the mission ends. It also teaches the fishing mechanic that the later fishing challenge (Baited My Tackle) builds on, so pay attention to how casting and reeling work here.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. Story chapters unlock in order, and the trophy pops when the chapter's final mission ends. If you rush the main story, the side content of Chapter 1 (activities and collectibles that appear early) is still there afterwards in free roam, so there is no need to 100% a chapter before moving on.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. The trophy is tied to the chapter's final mission, so keep playing the gold story markers until the chapter closes. New activities and stranger strands tend to open as chapters progress — check the map for new icons after each chapter ends.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. By this point the map is mostly open, so it is a good moment to clear the side strands and activities that have piled up (the stranger missions, the shooting range, the first collectibles) before the story pushes into Chapter 4.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4. This is the last chapter before the finale, so before starting the final mission, finish any story-adjacent content you care about: the stranger strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) and the partner missions all feed trophies of their own.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. It unlocks after Chapter 4, and the trophy pops when the mission — and the story — ends. It is the only gold story trophy, so it is also the natural point to switch from the story to the clean-up: after the credits, free roam stays open for everything that is left.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission. Play it through to the end and the trophy pops with the mission-complete screen. Named-mission trophies like this one are the game's way of marking story beats, so if a mission name does not ring a bell yet, keep following the gold story markers.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a named story mission — a heist, so expect a setup and a payoff in the same mission chain. Complete it and the trophy pops. Heist missions are usually the longest in a chapter, so stock up on ammo and armour at an Ammu-Nation before starting.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named story mission. Complete it to the end of the mission and the trophy pops. Like the other named-mission trophies, it is unmissable as long as you play the story — it only asks that you finish the mission.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission. Play it through and the trophy pops on completion. If you are tracking the story trophies in order, this one sits with the other mid-story mission trophies — check the checklist to see which named missions you have already cleared.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a named story mission set around the airport (VCIA is Vice City International Airport). Complete it and the trophy pops. The airport also matters for Catch Me If You Can, so while you are in the area, keep the airport's layout in mind for later.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a named story mission. Complete it and the trophy pops. The name suggests a big set-piece, so expect a longer mission — bring full armour and a stocked weapon wheel before starting it.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: 100% completion is the long grind: story missions, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and the miscellaneous checklist the game tracks under Stats. Open the in-game Stats menu to see the 100% checklist and what is still missing — the game itself tells you what counts. Leave this for last and work through it with this guide's checklist: every other trophy feeds into it, and the platinum follows immediately after.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game Stats menu (100% checklist)

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Stunts are the game's driving feats — stunt jumps, near misses, drifts and air time — and the counter sits in the Stats menu. The fastest way to rack them up is to chain stunt jumps off ramps and jumps around the city on a fast bike, which gives big air time, and to keep drifting through corners. It is a pure volume trophy: 250 sounds like a lot, but stunts happen naturally while driving, and a dedicated session of jump-hunting finishes it quickly.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game Stats menu (stunt counter)

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: There are 9 activity types in the game — the races, fishing, the shooting range, arcade games, drone races, bowling, meditation, hunting and the other map activities. Open the Activities section of the map or pause menu to see the types, and try each one once: you only need to sample them, not win or finish them. This is a good early trophy because it tours the side content and shows you what else is worth chasing.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game Activities menu (activity types)

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The Shooting Range has 42 challenges across the weapon types, and each one needs a gold medal — that means both speed and accuracy, not just hitting the targets. Start with the pistol challenges to learn the scoring, then work through the weapon types in order; the range tracks your medal per challenge, so you can see which ones still need gold. Use the range's own practice runs to learn each target layout before going for the timed gold run.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI Shooting Range (in-game medal tracking)

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations. You need one win at each location, so the job is to learn 14 short courses. Fly each course once to learn the gates, then race it for the win — drones handle differently from cars, so brake early for tight gates and cut corners where the course allows. The map marks the race locations, so work through them region by region.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game map (Top Fun race locations)

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different race events — each distinct race counts once, so repeating the same race does not help. Races are scattered across Leonida on land, and the race menu shows which ones you have already won. Pick the shorter circuits first and use the fastest car you own for its class; a win is a win, whatever the margin.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game race menu (won races)

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is a fishing rival: beat him in a fishing challenge. The opening mission (Gone Fishing) teaches casting and reeling — the challenge is the same mechanic under pressure. Watch the line tension, reel in steady bursts rather than holding the button down, and let the fish run when the tension spikes. The challenge is repeatable, so a lost round costs nothing but time.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI fishing (taught in the Gone Fishing mission)

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish any one arcade game at an arcade cabinet. You only need to complete a game, not beat a high score — pick the shortest cabinet game you find and play it through to its end screen. Arcades are marked on the map, and this trophy pairs naturally with trying the activity types for Master of None.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game map (arcade locations)

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of the stranger contacts whose mission strand runs through the game. Play his missions in order until the strand's final mission, and the trophy pops when it ends. Stranger strands unlock as the story progresses, so if Andy's icon is not on the map yet, keep playing the story chapters first.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand is another stranger mission chain. Follow his missions to their final one and finish it for the trophy. The name hints at a boat, so expect the finale to involve the water — keep a boat or a fast car handy when you take the last mission.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand ends with his final mission. Play through his missions in order and the trophy pops at the end of the last one. Stranger strands are easy to miss if you rush the story, so check the map for stranger icons after every chapter.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands — not just 8 missions, but 8 entire chains from first meeting to finale. Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have a strand with its own final-mission trophy, and there are more strangers across Leonida to find. The map's stranger icons are the starting points; finish a strand before starting the next one so you can track which of the 8 are done.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game map (stranger icons)

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand ends with his final mission. Work through his missions in order and the trophy pops when the last one ends. If his missions stop appearing, the strand is probably gated behind story progress — play the next chapter and check the map again.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's strand ends with his final mission. Finish his missions in order and the trophy pops at the end. Tyrone is one of the five named stranger contacts with a final-mission trophy, so clearing all five is most of the way to the 8 strands Strangers & Freaks needs.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: There are 18 meditation spots across Leonida. Meditation is a quiet activity: find a spot, start the meditation and let it finish. The spots are spread over the whole state, so this pairs well with exploring all 52 areas for The Goodtime State — meditate whenever you pass a spot instead of making 18 separate trips.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game map (meditation spots)

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret asks you to hunt a unique animal — a one-of-a-kind target, not a regular hunt. Follow Bret's strand to the hunt, track the animal the way the game teaches (signs, tracks, calls), and take the shot when you have a clear one. Bring a scoped rifle and approach from downwind; a spooked unique animal can cost you a long walk back.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida in sets, and you need 3 complete sets. Cards are tucked into interiors, rooftops and out-of-the-way corners — the kind of places you only find by exploring on foot. The collection menu shows which sets you have finished and which cards are still missing from each set, so use it to plan your routes instead of wandering blind.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game collection menu (card sets)

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It is the game's photo check-in: 100 locations across Leonida where you take the WAiNK shot. The counter is in the collection menu, and the map marks the spots you have found. It is a long tail trophy — do it steadily as you explore for The Goodtime State's 52 areas, and save the last few for a dedicated sweep with the map.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game map (WAiNK locations)

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Challenges are the game's checklist goals — small feats across driving, combat, exploration and activities — and you need 50 of them. The challenges menu lists them all with your progress, so open it early and let it steer your play: many challenges complete themselves while you chase other trophies. It is a clean-up trophy by nature, so don't grind it first — tick it off as the rest of the list falls.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game Challenges menu

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. The trick is the escape, not the stars: break line of sight, get out of the search area, and stay out of sight until the stars clear. Use the alleys and the water — a boat or a fast car through the canals breaks pursuit faster than a straight-line chase. Your partner has to be with you when the stars clear.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row — and the wanted level must stay alive through all three, so don't lose the cops between robberies. Plan a route of three shops close together, hit them fast, and keep moving: the wanted level is the timer, and the cops are the pressure. If the stars clear after the second shop, the chain breaks and you start over.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 distinct vehicles — entering or driving a vehicle you have not found before adds it to the count. Variety is the point: cars, bikes, boats, planes and the odd special vehicle all count, and the vehicle menu shows what you have discovered. Drive everything you see, and check the menu to find which classes you are missing.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game vehicle menu (discovered vehicles)

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is the game's slow-down aiming mode. To take down 5 enemies in one use, you need a group clustered together — a gang shootout or a police response is the place to try it. Trigger Combat Focus with a high-capacity weapon, work through the group quickly while time is slowed, and don't let the mode run out before the fifth target drops. If the group scatters, back out and try the next fight.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is Vice City International Airport, and the trophy wants an unscheduled departure — leave the airport by a route no passenger would use. Get a vehicle onto the runway area and take off down it, or find another way out through the airfield's edge. Expect a wanted level for trespassing, so bring a fast vehicle and a plan to lose the cops afterwards.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The Rhino is the game's tank, and this trophy is tied to dealing with one. Rhinos show up when the military responds at high wanted levels, so build the heat until one rolls in, then handle it — the description's joke is the hint that the tank itself is the point. Bring explosives and cover, and don't try it on foot in the open.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth job, not a smash-and-grab. Case the store first: watch the guard patrols and the cameras, enter quietly, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If a guard spots you, the attempt fails, so back out and try again rather than shooting your way out.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Vault robberies are the big heists of the open world: each one needs a plan to get in, crack the vault, and get out clean with the cops on the way. Do them one at a time and escape fully before starting the next — the count is per completed escape, not per attempt.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks run set routes around Leonida. Stop one, crack it open, take the cash and escape. The classic approach is to block the truck with your own vehicle, deal with the guards, and blow the rear doors — then lose the wanted level before you spend anything. The truck routes repeat, so if one attempt goes wrong, another truck will come along.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Leonida has 52 named areas, and you need to set foot in all of them. The map shows which areas you have visited, so the job is a road trip: drive the highways, then sweep the backroads, the islands and the swamps. It pairs with the meditation spots, the WAiNK locations and the vehicle discoveries — explore thoroughly once instead of making separate trips for each.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game map (visited areas)

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Nine gangs run illegal operations around Leonida, and you need to rob one operation belonging to each of them. Each gang holds different territory, so this trophy is also a tour of the state's underworld — hit one operation per gang and move on. Expect each gang to fight back, and expect a wanted level afterwards.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, find a bar with a view of the water, and order a cocktail. The description names the place, so this one is a simple visit: sit, drink, and enjoy the view. It is one of the quiet lifestyle trophies — a breather between the heists.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Take a vehicle inside a showroom and smash your way out through the glass — the classic GTA exit. Pick a showroom with a big front window, get the car moving inside, and drive straight out through the glass. The wanted level that follows is part of the fun; lose it afterwards.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and play a game of bowling — follow-through is the hint, so finish the game properly rather than walking out mid-frame. Bowling is one of the 9 activity types, so this also counts towards Master of None if you have not tried it yet.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game map (Kolt & Associates bowling alley)

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This trophy's description is deliberately cryptic — it is tied to a partnership moment with mass appeal. Keep playing the partner activities (the missions and jobs you do with your partner, like Hot Together and Retail Therapy) and it will pop from one of those milestones. If it has not popped by the time the partner content is done, it is one to revisit during clean-up.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: PSN tracks a count to 500 for this one: the choices you make across the game add up. Dialogue choices, approach choices in missions, and decisions in side content all count towards it, so play naturally and make choices instead of skipping through them. It is a volume trophy that fills up over a full playthrough — check the counter in the Stats menu if you want to see how far along you are.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game Stats menu (choice counter)

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed at something on your second try. The trophy's joke is the clue: fail an activity or a challenge once, then succeed at it on the immediate retry. If you are a careful player who rarely fails, the shooting range is the easiest place to arrange it — miss a gold run once, then nail it on the next attempt.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange in the world — a random event, a weird encounter, or something that does not fit. Leonida is full of odd sights if you wander off the main roads: strange lights, odd characters, unexplained happenings. Explore the backroads and the swamps at night and keep your eyes open; this one finds you when you are looking around.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a melee drive-by. Drive slowly past a pedestrian, swing the melee weapon from the driver's seat, and connect. Pick a quiet street with a lone pedestrian and a slow car so you can line the swing up; the trophy pops on the hit.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are dirty cash from robberies and heists, and your contacts launder them for clean money. Earn $250,000 through laundering — the counter tracks the laundered total, not your bank balance. Robberies (shops, trucks, vaults) are the source of Marked Bills, so this trophy fills up naturally while you chase the robbery trophies; launder regularly instead of sitting on a pile of bills.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game contacts (laundering)

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — clothes, weapons, vehicles, food, anything the shops sell. The counter is cumulative spending, so it fills up as you play; by the time you have bought good weapons and a few cars, you will be most of the way there. If you are short at the end, the expensive shops (vehicles, jewellery) close the gap fast.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are for sale around Leonida, marked on the map once you can afford them — and they are also where you store the vehicles you discover for Whip It Good and register for On the Spot. Buy them as you can afford them; the last few are the expensive ones, so save the money you earn from heists and laundering for them.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI in-game map (garage properties for sale)

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app lets you register vehicles you find. Register 10 different vehicles through the app — drive a vehicle you have discovered, open the app and register it. It pairs with Whip It Good's 100 discovered vehicles and the 8 garages: discover a vehicle, register it in the app, store it in a garage.
sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation, via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
GTA VI Scooter Bros app (in-game phone)
